text:
laura: quick spike idea: instead of moving big ownership blobs for demote/evict, we emit a tiny per-prefix "vEpoch" and a compact tombstone bitset. vEpoch increments on demote. readers compare vEpoch to local and decide stale behavior.

omar: sounds similar to vslot but what's the tombstone bitset for?

laura: tombstone marks recently-evicted subranges inside a prefix (for large prefixes with many keys). avoids full rehydrate for partial hot ranges. the owner keeps a small LRU of tombstone windows.

maria: correctness q: if a writer races and commits during demote, can we return non-monotonic views? how do we maintain linearizability for strict tenants?

laura: two-pronged: 1) every write carries a local writeSeq (wseq) monotonic per prefix. 2) wire includes headers: X-VEpoch: <u64>, X-WSeq: <u64>, X-Tombos: <base64-bitmask> (optional). read validation: if X-VEpoch > local_epoch -> validate wseq >= local_min_wseq else trigger strong-read. that preserves RW ordering without heavy handshake for most cases.

ken: can you show the fast path flow? ops will ask.

laura: sure:
```
client read -> shard cache miss -> owner responds with {data, vEpoch, wSeq, tombos} -> local compares vEpoch
if vEpoch == local_epoch -> serve
if vEpoch > local_epoch and wSeq >= local_min_wseq -> tentative serve (mark stale-maybe)
if vEpoch > local_epoch and wSeq < local_min_wseq -> refetch strong copy from owner (or proxy to primary)
```

omar: what about multi-tenant shards where many prefixes demote at once? tombstone bitset updates could be noisy. we need rate-limits and fanout controls.

jia: agree. limit per-shard tombstone broadcasts to N/sec and coalesce repeated bumps into a single vEpoch increment window (e.g., 100ms). also use an exponential jitter for client rehydration to avoid stampedes.

maria: test matrix: 1) late-writer injection where writer wins after vEpoch bump; 2) heavy demote storms across tenants; 3) partial-prefix rehydrates with tombstone masks. we should simulate with a 20-node cluster and 10k prefixes.

ken: metrics to add: vepoch_increments, tombstone_updates/sec, tentative_serves/sec, strong_refetch_rate, rehydrate_jitter_failures. also surface per-tenant strict_mode.

laura: UX: admin API to read per-prefix vEpoch and tombstone density; console heatmap would show prefixes with repeated vEpoch churn.

omar: semantics question: when we coalesce bumps, do we lose determinism for ordering? e.g., two rapid demotes might compress into one vEpoch tick and hide one demote event. is that acceptable?

laura: it's acceptable for the optimistic fast path: coalescing only affects metadata churn, not correctness, because wSeq carries precise ordering. strong reads still consult authoritative owner with exact history. coalesce is purely an optimization to reduce noise.

jia: rollout plan: feature-flagged; default off for Dedicated customers. enable in staging with small canary, exercise strict_mode path. add unit tests for bitset encoding/decoding and wSeq compare logic.

deploy-bot: canary/vEpoch-tombstone -> staging queued (job 9801) :rocket:

maria: also discuss backup/restore: tombstone state must be replayable. encode tombstone deltas as append-only events so we can reconstruct during leader-election.

ken: operational playbook: if tombstone density spikes, auto-lower tombstone retention and force tombstone compaction. surface alert when tentative_serves > 0.5% of reads for > 5m.

omar: small nit: include X-VEpoch and X-WSeq in stdout logs for correlation. include sample pprof to inspect tombstone mem overhead.

laura: will draft a short RFC and attach sim harness, wire proto, and test plan. target PR tomorrow; ping if you want to review.

ken: i'll help with the sim and dashboards. jia can help with rate-limit knobs.

jia: on it. thanks everyone.
